description.narrative:
On the morning of 10 August 2026, a powerful 7,4 earthquake with a 96km depth struck western Colombia with its epicentre in the department of Chocó. Shaking was felt across Colombia, as well as in Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama. More than 18 aftershocks have been recorded, including one of magnitude 4.8 M near San José del Palmar shortly after the main earthquake.
The earthquake was felt across at least 16 departments, prompting the activation of the National Disaster Risk Management System, reports include collapsing and severely damaged buildings in major cities like Cali, Quibdó and Pereira. Preliminary figures put the injuries at over 4,000, with over 300 casualties. On 12th August, IFRC Launched an Emergency Appeal for 25M CHF, targeting 24,000 people.
